must_include_names: Extract from the EDGAR document URL
expect.note: the three input modes' Extract buttons carry three different accessible names

provenance: M41, postmortem shape S3: at demo time the inspector's three input modes each rendered a button whose role and accessible name were exactly `button` / "Extract", so any plan targeting it resolved to 3 matches — the ambiguity shape M38 owns. sec-10k-extract's legibility row gave the three buttons distinct `aria-label`s, and this case measures that on the snapshot of the build that is deployed (`git_sha` `5a44758598f5`): three names, three elements, nothing to narrow. Watched RED first by stripping the three `aria-label` attributes out of the fixture, which is the demo page shape: `{"starved_by_chrome": ["Extract the selected committed fixture", "Extract the uploaded filing", "Extract from the EDGAR document URL"]}` — see `triage.red_first`.

triage.red_first: with the three `aria-label` attributes removed from the fixture — the demo page shape, three buttons all named "Extract" — the case reports {"starved_by_chrome": ["Extract the selected committed fixture", "Extract the uploaded filing", "Extract from the EDGAR document URL"], "n_elements": 60} and fails.
triage.note: S3 is fixed PAGE-SIDE on this one page, and this case pins only that. The capability gap behind it — what the resolver does when a real page offers three identical accessible names — is unchanged and stays with M38/ADR-026, whose own cases (`resolver-refuses-narrowing-a-click` and the D29 set) grade it. Nothing in `src/browser/` moved for this case, and nothing should have (CLAUDE.md rule 6: owning the target site is not an exemption).
